entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Demetrius of Esztergom (1250-1387) was a Hungarian cardinal and politician who played a pivotal role in the medieval politics of Eastern Europe. As archbishop of Esztergom and bishop of Zagreb and Transylvania, he served as chancellor to the Hungarian king, exerting significant influence on the kingdom's governance and ecclesiastical affairs.


He was a key figure in the Council of Basel (1431-1449), where he collaborated with other prominent theologians and politicians to address the theological and ecclesiastical disputes of the time.


Demetrius' legacy can be seen in the establishment of the University of Esztergom, which became a center of learning and intellectual inquiry in the region.


In his later years, Demetrius played a crucial role in the negotiations between the Kingdom of Hungary and the Ottoman Empire, seeking to secure a peaceful resolution to the conflicts between the two powers.


The importance of Demetrius' diplomatic efforts was underscored by his subsequent appointment as a cardinal, a position he held until his death in 1387.
